title: Wuhu Island Was Miyamoto's 10-Year Pet Project
hook: Shigeru Miyamoto spent more than ten years on one idea: an island everyone would recognize. It started out as plain old Wii Fit Island, became Wuhu Island in Wii Sports Resort, and this week it reopened on Switch 2. What was your go-to Wii Sports Resort game?
script: Did you know the island in Nintendo's new sports game was Shigeru Miyamoto's pet project for more than ten years? Miyamoto called it his island concept. The idea was one place that everyone knows, where all sorts of different games could happen. Nintendo first tried the idea in Wii Fit, which used a large island as its backdrop. Back then it was simply called Wii Fit Island. In two thousand nine, Wii Sports Resort polished that island up, turned it into a holiday resort, and named it Wuhu Island. Miyamoto said the goal was to turn a location into a kind of character, maybe even a franchise of its own. It worked. Wuhu Island went on to host Pilotwings Resort on the 3DS and two race tracks in Mario Kart 7. Wii Sports Resort itself sold more than thirty three million copies. The original Wii Sports did even better at about eighty three million, mostly because it came bundled with the Wii outside Japan. And this week Nintendo reopened the resort. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort launched on Switch 2 on October twenty second with twelve sports, and the island is back at the center of it. Which Wii Sports Resort game was your favorite, the swordplay or the bowling? Follow for more gaming history.
